Article Title: FSSAI steps up festive food crackdown as adulteration raids intensify
Article Text:
The regulator has specifically identified milk and milk products, sweets, snacks and savouries, edible oil, beverages and ghee for heightened scrutiny.

NEW DELHI: With festive demand for sweets and milk products rising, food safety authorities have stepped up enforcement across the country, with thousands of kilograms of suspected adulterated food already seized or destroyed in Delhi-NCR. The Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI) has now directed all states and Union territories to intensify inspections and sampling during Navratri and Diwali.In Delhi alone, food safety teams have destroyed more than 4,100 kg of suspected adulterated khoya and paneer during enforcement action last month, while samples of khoya, paneer, chhena and ghee are being collected from markets for testing.In neighbouring Mewat, officials have seized and destroyed more than 10,000 kg of adulterated paneer in last months, with around 50 raids conducted in areas identified as production hubs. Officials said the supply chain extends to Jaipur, Mathura, Gurugram, Faridabad and Delhi, raising concerns over the movement of adulterated paneer into the wider National Capital Region.Against this backdrop, FSSAI on September 29 directed food safety authorities across the country to step up surveillance and enforcement against adulterated, counterfeit and unsafe food products during the festive season.The regulator has specifically identified milk and milk products, sweets, snacks and savouries, edible oil, beverages and ghee for heightened scrutiny.States have been asked to conduct inspections and sampling at identified hotspots and sensitive locations. The directive also asks authorities to record inspection, sampling and outcome data on the Food Safety Compliance System (FoSCoS) and Food Safety Compliance through Regular Inspection and Sampling of Food (FoSCoRIS) on a real-time basis.The national directive also allows states to focus on products specific to local consumption patterns, including kuttu atta and singhada atta in northern and western regions.
Article Summary: With festive demand for sweets and milk products rising, food safety authorities have stepped up enforcement. Thousands of kilograms of suspected adulterated food already seized or destroyed in delhi-ncr. Food safety and standards authority of india (fssai) has now directed all states and union territories to intensify inspections and sampling during navratri and diwali.

Article Title: Delhi Police registers 3 FIRs over protests demanding CEC Gyanesh Kumar's resignation
Article Text:
No individual or organisation has been named as an accused in the FIRs

NEW DELHI: Delhi Police on Saturday registered three FIRs in connection with Friday’s protests by student organisations, political parties and civil society activists who attempted to gather at Jantar Mantar demanding the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar.Two FIRs were registered at Parliament Street police station and one at Connaught Place police station, a senior police officer said. The cases invoke Section 223 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), which deals with alleged disobedience of an order duly promulgated by a public servant.No individual or organisation has been named as an accused in the FIRs, the officer said. However, details of organisers and organisations that proposed or participated in the demonstrations have been included in the contents of the cases.The FIRs follow a day of protests across central Delhi, where thousands of opposition activists, students and youth organisation members attempted to march towards Jantar Mantar. Police detained around 1,000 protesters as they tried to cross barricades and reach the designated protest site.The demonstrations involved the Aam Aadmi Party (AAP), All India Students' Association (AISA), Students' Federation of India (SFI), National Students' Union of India (NSUI), Indian Youth Congress (IYC) and other organisations.Protesters were demanding Kumar’s resignation over alleged irregularities in the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls and alleged mass deletion of voters.Police had repeatedly announced that gatherings were not permitted at Jantar Mantar. Protesters were stopped at several locations, including Firoz Shah Road and Ashoka Road, with some attempting to push past barricades. AISA president Neha Bora and several other activists were among those stopped.AAP leaders Saurabh Bharadwaj, Atishi and Sanjeev Jha were detained, while Rajya Sabha MP Sanjay Singh was stopped while heading towards the protest. NSUI president Vinod Jakhar and activists from SFI and other student groups were also detained.Security was stepped up across central Delhi, with around 5,000 Delhi Police and paramilitary personnel deployed. Entry and exit gates at 12 metro stations were closed and internet services were suspended in parts of central Delhi amid the protests.
Article Summary: Delhi police on saturday registered three firs in connection with friday’s protests. Demonstrators attempted to gather at jantar mantar demanding resignation of chief election commissioner gyanesh kumar. No individual or organisation has been named as an accused in the firs.

Article Title: Nearly half of India’s medical colleges fail to comply with NMC disability-unit directive
Article Text:
Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Nearly half of India’s medical colleges (44.5%) have failed to set up Enabling Units mandated by the National Medical Commission for students with benchmark disabilities. Of 798 colleges, 355 remain non-compliant, with several naming sanitation inspectors, residents, tutors and head clerks as single points of contact, according to an affidavit filed by the Commission in the Supreme Court on Tuesday.At Maharashtra Government Medical College, Nandurbar, a sanitation inspector, has been designated as the coordinator of the Enabling Unit. Other colleges have named residents, tutors and head clerks as points of contact.Dr Satendra Singh, disability-rights activist and doctor associated with Doctors with Disabilities: Agents of Change, questioned the choice of personnel for the role. “It’s unheard of for a sanitation inspector or head clerk to be made in-charge of such a committee in a medical college. They have neither the designated administrative or academic responsibility for undergraduate or postgraduate training nor the training or authority to deal with disability accommodation, clinical training, patient safety or assessment.He added, “They cannot take or escalate decisions on postings, duty hours, assistive devices, accessible infrastructure, examination accommodations or clinical-rotation modifications. Tutors and residents are also a floating population, often at an institution for only a limited period. How would a postgraduate student in pharmacology, who may not even be an alumnus of that institution, know what assistance a wheelchair-using medical student needs in an operation theatre or have the authority to direct the theatre staff?”The NMC circular does not prescribe a doctor or clinical faculty member as the single point of contact. It does, however, assign the Enabling Unit responsibility for reasonable accommodation, academic and clinical support, barrier-free access, coordination, record-keeping and information dissemination.The compliance exercise was undertaken following the Supreme Court’s August 4, 2026 order in Anmol vs Union of India, which directed the NMC to seek college-wise compliance with its July 27 circular through Deans and Principals.The court warned that if colleges failed to respond or follow the directions, “a serious view will be taken against the individual colleges.”The NMC’s affidavit said 515 of 798 colleges had responded by September 28: 443 reported full compliance, 26 partial or ongoing compliance, and 46 submitted only the committee-constitution order. As many as 283 colleges did not respond. Majority of NMC-designated medical assessment boards and appellate boards themselves fail to comply, despite NMC warning that “serious view” would be takenThe commission had set September 10 as the deadline and issued reminders on September 23 and 24, the latter warning that late submissions would not be accepted and show-cause notices would follow. Colleges were required to provide details of the unit, its members and POC, functionality, accessibility, communication to students, records and compliance status.
Article Summary: Of 798 colleges, 355 remain non-compliant, with several naming sanitation inspectors, residents, tutors and head clerks as single points of contact. At maharashtra government medical college, nandurbar, a sanitation inspector has been designated as the coordinator of the enabling unit.

Article Title: CJP protest: Scuffle breaks out near Shiv Sena Bhavan as supporters return from stir; watch
Article Text:
A scuffle erupted near Shiv Sena Bhavan in Dadar after a protest





MUMBAI: A scuffle broke out near Shiv Sena Bhavan in Dadar after supporters of the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) returned from a protest at Shivaji Park.A video from the spot shows protesters arguing, with some allegedly hitting each other.The situation soon turned physical, prompting police to intervene and disperse those involved. Mumbai Police later said the situation was under control and peaceful.The incident followed a CJP protest at Shivaji Park over the party’s demands concerning Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar.Before the protest, a Dadar resident had opposed the demonstration. “They are doing it forcefully. This protest should not take place,” the resident said, adding that such demonstrations disturb peace in the area.The CJP has been demanding Kumar’s resignation and changes to the functioning and appointment process of the Election Commission. The Election Commission currently lists Gyanesh Kumar as the Chief Election Commissioner.Mumbai Police had earlier denied permission for the CJP to hold its October 2 protest at Shivaji Park. The party later announced a “Jail Bharo Andolan”.Meanwhile, a 75-year-old Thane resident died after suffering a heart attack while attending the CJP protest at Shivaji Park on Friday evening.The deceased was identified as Gopalakrishna Subbaiya Pillai, a resident of Dosti West County in Thane.Pillai arrived at Shivaji Park around 4.30pm to attend the protest. Around 5pm, he complained of chest pain. His friend and police personnel at the spot helped take him to Sushrusha Hospital in Shivaji Park.Police personnel tried to revive him with CPR before he was taken to the hospital, where he died while undergoing treatment. Police said doctors attributed his death to a heart attack.
Article Summary: A scuffle broke out near shiv sena bhavan in dadar after supporters of the cockroach janta party (cjp) returned from a protest at shivaji park. The situation soon turned physical, prompting police to intervene and disperse those involved. Mumbai police later said the situation was under control and peaceful.

Article Title: Of 97 left out in Goa, 88 are back, 3 others are Portuguese citizens: EC
Article Text:
Goans born before 1961 in former Portuguese territories, as well as their kids and grandchildren, can apply for a Portuguese passport based on a citizen card issued by the Portuguese authorities after verifying their birth/descent documents.

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: The office of the Goa chief electoral officer on Thursday said 88 of the 97 voters in the state whose names could not be included in the roll due to an alleged ECINet issue have been added back after their duly filled Form 6 was accepted. However, he also revealed that three of these 97 electors are Portuguese passport holders while six others were electors currently based outside India."In respect of voters who are currently residing outside India, officials are making efforts to establish and maintain contact with them for necessary action," the CEO said while sharing the status report on the 97 cases on X.Section 9 of the Constitution disallows dual citizenship. Goans born before 1961 in former Portuguese territories, as well as their kids and grandchildren, can apply for a Portuguese passport based on a citizen card issued by the Portuguese authorities after verifying their birth/descent documents. Portugal recognises dual citizenship; however, since dual citizenship is not allowed in India, anybody who acquires a foreign passport must surrender his Indian passport.As per Sec 9 of the Citizenship Act, 1955, a person's Indian citizenship automatically ceases upon acquiring foreign citizenship.Thus, three of the Portuguese passport holders in Goa may be classified as non-citizens, making them ineligible to be enrolled as Indian electors, said a source.Incidentally, Portuguese passport holders form 3% of the cohort of 97 electors for which the Goa CEO had repeatedly written to the EC after the ERO could not add them back via ERONet, leading the ECs to also raise questions on why access for such changes was 'centralised' and not available to the field officers. The issue was further amplified by the opposition parties after The Indian Express reported on the alleged internal notes of the election commissioners in this regard.EC sources on Thursday said the due diligence by the ERO the second time around may have served the purpose of SIR, as it is aimed at eliminating ineligible persons from the voters' list. Also, the fact that the issue was detected at the ERO level proves that the absolute right to add or delete a voter, based on verification, remains with the field officers, an EC officer told TOI.
Article Summary: 88 of the 97 voters in the state whose names could not be included in the roll due to an alleged ecinet issue have been added back. Three of these 97 electors are portuguese passport holders while six others were electors currently based outside india.

Article Title: Delhi riots case: High court rejects bail pleas Of Umar Khalid, Sharjeel Imam
Article Text:
Umar Khalid, Sharjeel Imam denied bail by high court

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: The Delhi High Court has refused to grant bail to Umar Khalid and Sharjeel Imam in the UAPA case related to the 2020 Delhi riots.Senior Advocate Trideep Pais, appearing for Umar Khalid, submitted that there had been three “small changes in circumstances” since the earlier proceedings. He also referred the court to a Supreme Court judgment in support of his submissions.Pais pointed out that charges have not yet been framed in the case and, consequently, prosecution witnesses are yet to be examined. The court also noted that the charges were yet to be framed.Pais further submitted that a Special Leave Petition (SLP) is pending before the Supreme Court and that the trial court has indicated it would await the Supreme Court’s order. He then continued his submissions by referring to the Supreme Court judgment.Khalid and Imam had approached the Delhi High Court earlier this year after their bail applications were dismissed by the trial court for the third time on July 4. Imam was arrested in the case on August 25, 2020, while Khalid was arrested on September 13, 2020.The Delhi Police has opposed their bail pleas in the high court, asserting that the two were “masterminds” of the riots, PTI reported.The police argued that they could not seek bail on parity with other co-accused, stating that the Supreme Court had earlier categorised them as being part of the “command authority” and held that their “risk profiles” justified “continuing detention”.The police also argued that the present bail pleas were in the teeth of the Supreme Court’s January 5 order, which directed them to seek release only after the examination of protected witnesses was completed or after one year, whichever was earlier.On July 4, the trial court rejected Khalid’s bail application, saying it had “no option but to follow” the Supreme Court’s January 5 order and could therefore neither entertain the plea nor grant him relief.On September 2, 2025, a Delhi High Court division bench denied bail to Khalid and Imam. The Supreme Court upheld the verdict on January 5 but granted relief to co-accused Gulfisha Fatima, Meeran Haider, Shifa Ur Rehman, Mohammad Saleem Khan and Shadab Ahmad.A bench of Justice Aravind Kumar and Justice NV Anjaria had observed that there was a prima facie case against Khalid and Imam under the UAPA.On May 22, the Supreme Court granted six months’ interim bail to co-accused Abdul Khalid Saifi and Tasleem Ahmad, while referring to a larger bench the issue of prolonged incarceration of undertrials under the UAPA due to the stringent conditions for granting bail.
Article Summary: Umar khalid, sharjeel imam denied bail by high court in uapa case related to 2020 delhi riots. Delhi police has opposed their bail pleas in the high court, asserting that the two were ‘masterminds’ of the riots.

Article Title: Akhilesh Yadav's Rajya Sabha picks: Samajwadi Party's master strategy or 'PDA' contradiction?
Article Text:
SP chief Akhilesh Yadav has nominated Ram Gopal Yadav and Dhanraj Parimal Nathwani for the Rajya Sabha polls.

Why Nathwani?

The third nomination suspense

A rehearsal for 2027

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

A 'family' man, a corporate executive, a possible third candidate and a high-stakes numbers game: Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav 's Rajya Sabha strategy has a bit of a test run for the 2027 UP assembly polls?His two picks have an element of continuity and also surprise. But then there is also an element of contradiction vis-à-vis the strong PDA pitch which has been the backbone of his 2027 poll strategy. Little wonder, then, that talk of a third nominee has begun even without the numbers, raising the stakes from a routine Rajya Sabha contest to an early test of Akhilesh's 2027 strategy.For the two sure-shot Rajya Sabha seats in Uttar Pradesh, Akhilesh Yadav has paired a familiar Samajwadi Party face with a distinctly unfamiliar political profile. Alongside his uncle Ram Gopal Yadav, the SP has nominated Dhanraj Parimal Nathwani, a senior Reliance Industries executive whose father, Parimal Nathwani, is a four-time Rajya Sabha MP backed by the BJP-led NDA. The choice immediately puts two very different images of the SP on the same ticket: its established family name and a corporate, professional profile from outside its traditional ecosystem.Nathwani's nomination also raises a larger question about the SP's direction as it prepares for the 2027 assembly election.Is Nathwani's nomination an attempt to expand the SP's political appeal beyond its traditional social base, or does bringing a senior corporate executive into Parliament sit uneasily with a party increasingly building its politics for the 2027 polls around PDA, Pichhda, Dalit and Alpsankhyak? The question matters beyond the Rajya Sabha because the SP is simultaneously trying to project itself as the principal challenger to the BJP in Uttar Pradesh ahead of the 2027 assembly election.Akhilesh's second nomination is more than a surprise name on a candidate list. His corporate background gives the SP an opportunity to make a political argument it has not traditionally foregrounded. The party can present his candidature as evidence that its appeal is extending beyond its conventional political base and that people from the corporate and professional world now see the party as a credible political force.For a party preparing for 2027, that can also help reinforce a broader pitch around investment, jobs, industry and development alongside its social-justice agenda, which could become a significant part of the BJP and Yogi government's election campaign next year.Akhilesh, in fact, responded to queries over criticism of Nathwani's nomination by invoking Ram Manohar Lohia. "I think you should read about socialism again. I will give you a book by (Ram Manohar) Lohia," he said. He argued that socialist thought also talks about prosperity and equality and said governments across the country seek investment to generate economic growth."This time, it will be Lodhi vs Yogi (Adityanath)," he said on September 30.However, the same choice also produces a very different political reading.Akhilesh's electoral strategy for the 2027 polls has been heavily identified with PDA, and Nathwani is not an obvious representative of the social coalition that phrase describes. That gives the opposition an opening to question why a party seeking votes in the name of backward classes, Dalits and minorities has chosen a senior corporate executive for one of its two Rajya Sabha seats.Mayawati, in fact, used the same charge against the SP. "SP wants votes in the name of PDA, but makes mostly its own family members and big capitalists MPs and MLAs," she said in a post on X.State minister and Suheldev Bharatiya Samaj Party (SBSP) president Om Prakash Rajbhar also targeted Akhilesh, accusing him of repeatedly changing the framework for PDA. "Akhilesh Yadav keeps changing the PDA formula from time to time. Yesterday, he came up with the formula of a PDA family. 'P' now stands for 'Parivaar'," Rajbhar said, referring to Ram Gopal Yadav. "‘D’ stands for the 'Daulat', referring to Dhani Ram, who is affluent," Rajbhar said."Now, only 'A' remains, and he will bring in some criminal to represent it. The new PDA formula stands for 'Parivaar', 'Daulat' and 'Apradhi'," he added.The BJP, meanwhile, is watching Nathwani's nomination closely but has not mounted a similarly strong direct attack on the choice.The Uttar Pradesh assembly currently has 396 effective members after seven vacancies, putting the winning quota for a Rajya Sabha seat at 37 first-preference votes. The BJP has 255 MLAs, while the SP has 101 and Congress has two. The BJP's alliance partners include Apna Dal (S), RLD, SBSP and Nishad Party, giving the ruling camp a substantial numerical advantage. Broadly, the BJP-led camp is positioned to take the larger share of the 10 seats, while the SP-Congress combination has enough strength for two.The problem begins with the third candidate. The SP would need roughly nine additional first-preference votes to reach the quota for a third seat. That means Akhilesh cannot rely only on his existing alliance strength. He would have to attract support from outside it, potentially through smaller parties, independents or legislators willing to cross-vote.The suspense over that third candidate has now become central to the contest. SP MP Virendra Singh has said the party will field a third candidate, with the name to be decided and the nomination filed by October 5. Singh has also claimed that several BJP MLAs seeking SP tickets for the 2027 elections are in touch with the party.Akhilesh, meanwhile, has continued to leave room for political manoeuvring. Earlier in the day he described the Rajya Sabha election as "the time for coming together" and said it offered an opportunity to forget past mistakes and stand united with others on matters of principle.A day earlier, when asked whether the SP would field a third candidate, he declined to confirm the party's plans and said: "The BJP can do anything. They can field nine or even 10 candidates."The BJP, meanwhile, has made its own claims about SP legislators. Deputy CM Keshav Prasad Maurya has said that 25 SP MLAs are in contact with the BJP and warned that the party would "surprise" the SP.This Rajya Sabha election, along with the immediate parliamentary tally, will ultimately be about a strategic stress-test for 2027.In fielding Nathwani, Akhilesh Yadav is executing a high-stakes balancing act: attempting to reposition the Samajwadi Party as a pragmatic, investment-friendly government-in-waiting, without alienating the core PDA base that forms its electoral backbone. It is a gamble that risks handing opponents cheap ideological ammunition in exchange for broader institutional credibility and expanded corporate outreach.Whether this move is remembered as a masterstroke of political expansion or a self-inflicted ideological contradiction will not be decided in the corridors of the Rajya Sabha. It will be decided by how effectively Akhilesh manages the cross-currents - maintaining the confidence of his grassroots voters while proving that his vision for Uttar Pradesh can accommodate both social justice and corporate capital. The upcoming floor vote, and the potential fight for a third seat, will offer the first real glimpse of whether that strategy can hold.
Article Summary: Sp chief akhilesh yadav has nominated ram gopal yadav and dhanraj parimal nathwani for the rajya sabha polls. The choice immediately puts two very different images of the sp on the same ticket: its established family name and a corporate profile. The uttar pradesh assembly currently has 396 effective members after seven vacancies.

Article Title: Lawyers’ body forms panel to review SIR: Ex-SC, HC judges to examine ‘constitutional & statutory validity’
Article Text:
The panel will assess the SIR’s impact on eligible voters and hold public hearings to record the views of affected citizens.

A panel of five former Supreme Court and high court judges has been set up by a lawyers' body to examine the Election Commission ’s Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls, as the poll panel separately moves to identify and re-enrol voters left out during the exercise.The Lawyers Association for Constitution (LAFC) said the commission, headed by former Supreme Court judge Madan B Lokur, will examine the constitutional and statutory validity of the SIR, its methodology and its overall impact on eligible voters, reported PTI."The newly-formed independent commission of former judges on the Special Intensive Revision of the electoral roll will function with complete autonomy to examine the constitutional and statutory validity, methodology and overall impact of the SIR exercise on eligible voters," it said.The other members are former Supreme Court judge A K Patnaik, former chief justice of the Jammu and Kashmir High Court Badar Durrez Ahmad, and former judges Rekha Sharma and Anjana Prakash.Meanwhile, LAFC said senior lawyers including Kapil Sibal, Prashant Bhushan, Chander Uday Singh, Prashanto Chandra Sen, Raju Ramachandran, Rebecca Mammen John, Warisha Farasat and Vrinda Grover will provide strategic legal advice to the commission.The commission will examine whether eligible citizens were retained on the electoral roll and whether ineligible entries were appropriately excluded, the LAFC said.It plans to hold public hearings across the country, with full and regional benches travelling to different locations to record the views and testimonies of affected citizens, civil society organisations and experts.The LAFC said the commission would function with complete autonomy and have the final responsibility for its findings and recommendations.The panel's formation comes as the Election Commission has directed state poll officials to launch a special drive to identify and enrol valid voters who were left out after the SIR in states where the exercise has been completed.Under the drive, Booth Level Officers will compare current electoral rolls with pre-SIR lists to identify electors whose names were earlier included but later dropped. They will then conduct house-to-house verification of the identified voters.The BLOs have also been asked to collect Form 6 applications on the spot from eligible first-time voters and genuine left-out electors. The exercise is targeted for completion within a month, with each BLO expected to cover 20 to 25 electors a week.The move follows the Election Commission's September 26 decision to withdraw an additional SIR-related declaration attached to Form 6 in states where the revision has been completed. New applicants in these states will now submit the regular statutory Form 6.The additional declaration remains available in states and Union territories where SIR is still under way. Under it, new applicants are required to provide details linking themselves, their parents or grandparents to electoral rolls prepared during an earlier SIR.
Article Summary: The panel will assess the sir’s impact on eligible voters and hold public hearings to record the views of affected citizens. It comes as the poll panel separately moves to identify and re-enrol voters left out during the exercise.

Article Title: EC orders special drive to add genuine electors 'left out' during SIR
Article Text:
An EC official said an average 10% of 800-900 electors per booth were deleted through SIR. Thus, each BLO will have to verify enrolment eligibility of less than 100 'deleted' voters.

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: The Election Commission on Thursday ordered a special drive to identify and add back genuine electors who may have been "left out" during the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) drive completed in 20 states, besides facilitating first-time or young electors.As part of the drive - meant to percolate to the grassroots the message that the deletions made during SIR, if erroneous, can be undone at any time by simply filling up Form 6 (for fresh enrolment) - booth level officers (BLOs) will visit homes of electors who were there in the pre-SIR electoral roll but were not included in the current electoral roll. They will, during these visits, ascertain the present status of such electors and facilitate their enrolment through Form 6, wherever a person is found to be eligible. This could be due to a valid eligibility proof not submitted earlier, corrected mapping to roll from last SIR, return of a shifted voter at registered address, or a young voter who has turned 18 since SIR, etc, said an official."Voter enrolment is a continuous process and any person not yet enrolled in the electoral roll or whose name has got deleted can apply for enrolment at any point of time. The objective of the special drive is to identify and facilitate such electors," EC said in a letter to state chief electoral officers (CEOs) Thursday.This followed a meeting held by EC with state/UT CEOs on Tuesday.As per the decision taken by the full commission on Sept 26, no declaration will need to be attached with Form 6 during the special drive.Nearly 7.7 crore voters were deleted across 13 states covered in SIR's first two phases, though net deletions came to around 5.6 crore. In Phase 3, completed in seven states, net deletions total nearly 24 lakh.The special drive's timing is significant as it comes days after a report in The Indian Express report alleged that election commissioners S S Sandhu and Vivek Joshi had raised questions over the SIR process in internal notes. However, the EC, in a statement released after a full commission meeting on Sept 26, placed it on record that all decisions related to SIR were unanimously approved by the CEC and the commissioners.The opposition, however, continues to amplify the issue, "unilaterally" blaming CEC Gyanesh Kumar for a "flawed" SIR, "unauthorised" changes to Form 6 and allegedly limited access of field officers to ECINet for making changes.Sources in the EC, however, told TOI Friday that the special drive is only in furtherance of the repeated directions by CEC to BLOs that "not a single Indian citizen who has completed 18 years of age should be left out of electoral roll".An EC official said an average 10% of 800-900 electors per booth were deleted through SIR. Thus, each BLO will have to verify enrolment eligibility of less than 100 "deleted" voters. With the EC instructing BLOs on Friday to visit the homes of 20-25 electors per week, house-to-house outreach and verification is expected to last a month.BLOs who visit the houses of deleted electors shall indicate the present status of each such elector in a list of absent, permanently shifted, deceased, duplicate and foreigner electors prepared by them. Electors for whom Form 6 has been filled up will also be indicated.They will share this list with booth level agents (BLAs) of recognised political parties and with electoral registration officers (EROs), along with the filled-up Form 6 and their field verification report. ERO is the competent authority to decide on addition or deletion.At the end of this exercise, the booth-wise lists prepared as above will also be shared by the EROs with the representatives of the political parties, giving them a further opportunity to enable enrolment of any left-out electors.Booth-level camps shall be organised to facilitate submission of applications for enrolment. Special camps may also be organised for enrolment of people living in night shelters, labour colonies and also for homeless & marginalised persons.As part of SIR completed in 20 states, a list of ASDD voters was prepared by each BLO with the probable reason for non-inclusion of their names. This list was displayed at the notice board of respective panchayat bhawans/urban local bodies and offices of the BDOs/panchayat, shared with the BLAs and with the political parties and also uploaded on the CEO website.Thereafter, the draft was published and shared with the political parties and uploaded on the CEO website. The final electoral roll was published after decisions on the claims and objections by the EROs and includes the list of electors that were added or deleted after the draft publication.
Article Summary: The election commission on thursday ordered a special drive to identify and add back genuine electors who may have been "left out" during the special intensive revision (sir) drive completed in 20 states. The drive is meant to percolate to the grassroots the message that the deletions made during sir, if erroneous, can be undone at any time.

Article Title: Gandhi's first birthday in free India was no celebration: What happened on October 2, 1947
Article Text:
Freedom was just two months old and the country was still struggling to come to terms with Partition when Gandhi’s 78th birthday approached

A country in flames

What Gandhi did on his 78th birthday

'Today nobody listens to me'

'If I’m to die by the bullet of a mad man ...'

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: India wanted to celebrate Mahatma Gandhi on October 2, 1947. Gandhi, however, himself wanted no celebration at all.It was his first birthday in an independent India and, as it turned out, his last. Messages, flowers and greetings poured in from India and abroad. Jawaharlal Nehru, Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel and others came to meet him. But Gandhi, who turned 78 that day, was consumed by what was happening outside the walls of Birla House.Barely seven weeks had passed since Independence. Partition had displaced millions and triggered widespread communal violence across India and Pakistan.So when people wished Gandhi a long life, his response was not one of celebration."Where did the congratulations come in? Would it not be more appropriate to say condolences?" he asked.Later that day, Gandhi told those gathered for his prayer meeting: "For me today is the day of mourning. I am surprised and also ashamed that I am still alive."Freedom was just two months old and the country was still struggling to come to terms with Partition when Gandhi’s 78th birthday approached.Gandhi had already spent months confronting the violence.According to the Gandhi Heritage Portal, he left for Noakhali in November 1946 after communal violence erupted there and later began a barefoot march through affected villages, appealing for peace and Hindu-Muslim unity.His peace mission continued even when India became independent. The Gandhi Heritage Portal records that Gandhi stayed in riot-hit Calcutta in August 1947 and spent Independence Day fasting and praying rather than taking part in the celebrations.Violence followed Gandhi to Delhi. According to the Gandhi Heritage Portal, when he reached the capital on September 9, 1947, communal violence and refugee camps had made it impossible for him to stay at his usual accommodation at Valmiki Colony, and he moved into Birla House instead.From there, Gandhi continued holding prayer meetings and appealing for communal peace as tensions gripped the capital.According to historian Brijmohan Heda, October 2, 1947, was remembered by those who visited Gandhi that day as one of the most painful days of his life. While the country prepared to celebrate his birthday, Gandhi showed little interest in the celebrations and spent much of the day in prayer and spinning the charkha.At the morning prayer, Mirabehn decorated the space around Gandhi’s seat at Birla House with flowers arranged in the shape of an Om, the words 'Hey Ram' and a cross. Jawaharlal Nehru, Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel, Ghanshyamdas Birla and Indira Gandhi were among those present.Lady Mountbatten was among those who visited Gandhi later in the day and brought letters and telegrams sent to him from India and abroad.A special radio programme had also been planned to mark his birthday. When asked whether he would listen to the All India Radio programme, Gandhi made his choice clear. He said he would give greater importance to the 'rentio', the spinning wheel, than to the radio.Later in the evening, Gandhi suffered a bout of coughing. His doctors advised him to take penicillin, but he refused, saying Ramanama: the chanting of Lord Rama’s name was his 'sole remedy'.Consumed by the bloodshed around him, Gandhi used his prayer meeting address on October 2, 1947, to speak openly about his anguish.“Today is my birthday. I do not celebrate my birthday in the usual way. I would say that on this day we must fast, spin and pray. That, in my view, is the most appropriate way of celebrating one’s birthday,” Gandhi said.“For me today is the day of mourning. I am surprised and also ashamed that I am still alive. I am the same person whose word was honoured by the millions of the country. But today nobody listens to me,” he added. The remarks are recorded in the Collected Works of Mahatma Gandhi.Gandhi then spoke about the growing hostility towards Muslims and questioned what India would become if the violence continued.“You want only the Hindus to remain in India and say that none else should be left behind. You may kill the Muslims today; but what will you do tomorrow? What will happen to the Parsis and the Christians and then to the British?” he said.“Ever since I came to India I have made it my profession to work for communal harmony, and I wish that though our religions are different we may live in amity like brothers. But today we seem to have become enemies,” Gandhi said.Gandhi also said he had given up his earlier desire to live to the age of 125.“I have now stopped thinking about living for 125 years. I have stopped thinking in terms of 100 or even 90 years. I am entering my 79th year today; but even that pains me,” he said.He ended with an appeal against communal hatred: “If you really want to celebrate my birthday, it is your duty not to let anyone be possessed by madness and if there is any anger in your hearts you must remove it.”After the prayer meeting, Gandhi spoke to Sardar Patel in private and asked what “sin” he had committed to be kept alive to witness such horrors, an exchange also recounted by historian Ramachandra Guha.Just four months later, Gandhi was assassinated in New Delhi.On January 30, 1948, as he walked towards the evening prayer meeting at Birla House, Nathuram Godse approached him and fired three shots at close range. Gandhi died shortly afterwards. The Gandhi Heritage Portal records that he was shot while on his way to the prayer ground and received three bullets.Gandhi was 78 when he was killed. He had spent much of his life speaking against violence and urging Hindus and Muslims to live together peacefully.Just two days before his assassination, Gandhi had spoken about the possibility of being killed."If I’m to die by the bullet of a mad man, I must do so smiling. God must be in my heart and on my lips," he had said on January 28, 1948, according to a contemporary report published by 'The Hindu'.Four months earlier, on his last birthday, Gandhi had already spoken of losing his desire for a long life.The man who had once hoped to live for 125 years had finally seen India become independent. But on his first birthday in free India, the violence surrounding that freedom left him with little reason to celebrate.
Article Summary: October 2, 1947, was gandhi's first birthday in an independent india. Messages, flowers and greetings poured in from india and abroad. But gandhi, who turned 78 that day, was consumed by what was happening outside the walls of birla house. I am surprised and also ashamed that i am still alive.

Article Title: Himachal implements mandatory dress code for teachers in government CBSE schools
Article Text:
The dress code has been formulated as per the climatic conditions of Himachal Pradesh (Photo: ANI).

Himachal Pradesh implemented a mandatory dress code for teachers across 148 government CBSE schools on Thursday, attempting to create a more organised and professional learning environment.A notice dated September 10 explained that the prescribed dress code has been formulated "keeping in view the professional requirements of the teaching profession, uniformity in appearance and the climatic conditions of Himachal Pradesh."The dress code's colour palette includes light lilac, lilac purple and navy blue, with black prescribed for footwear and other specified accessories.The prescribed dress code offers female teachers three alternatives: a saree with a blazer, a kurta/kameez with pants, a plazo or salwar and a blazer, and a shirt and blazer with pants and a tie. For male teachers, however, only a single formal combination has been laid down: shirt with a tie, pants, and a blazer.According to the notice, the dress code is mandatory and will apply to all teachers, including principals, without exception, regardless of how they were recruited or engaged. This includes teachers whose services are being availed on an outsourced basis, for the time being.Reasonable adjustments may be allowed with the approval of the head of the institution in cases of medical necessity, disability or pregnancy.The state government also plans to open 100 new CBSE schools from the coming academic session, while roughly 2,000 teaching posts in CBSE schools have already been filled, PTI reported.To reinforce accountability, a system that logs teachers' attendance three times a day is also being brought in.Director of school education, Ashish Kohli, said the reforms had made a positive difference to the education sector, placing greater importance on quality education, equal opportunities, accountability and learning centred on students. He added that this had made Himachal Pradesh a role model for education reforms.
Article Summary: Himachal pradesh implemented a mandatory dress code for teachers across 148 government cbse schools on thursday. The prescribed dress code offers female teachers three alternatives: a saree with a blazer, a kurta/kameez with pants, a plazo or salwar and a blazers.

Article Title: Rahul Gandhi demands CEC Gyanesh Kumar’s resignation as protests erupt in Delhi, Mumbai
Article Text:
Rahul Gandhi hits out at Centre amid protests against CEC, invokes Mahatma Gandhi

Around 700 detained in Delhi

Protests in Mumbai and questions over SIR

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Leader of opposition in the Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi on Friday demanded the resignation of chief election commissioner Gyanesh Kumar as opposition parties, student groups and civil society organisations held protests in Delhi and Mumbai over alleged irregularities in the electoral-roll revision exercise.In a post on X on Gandhi Jayanti, the Raebareli MP said thousands of young people were protesting peacefully against what he called “vote theft” and alleged that hundreds had been detained.“Today is Gandhi Jayanti. And today, thousands of young people are on the streets against vote theft - peacefully, without violence, exercising their constitutional rights. Their demand is clear: Gyanesh Kumar must resign. Save democracy,” the Congress leader said.He alleged that the response of the “Modi-Shah government” had been to detain protesters.“And the Modi-Shah government's response? Boys and girls are being dragged off the streets. Hundreds are in custody. Their only crime is that they dared to question vote theft,” he said.Former Congress president also invoked Mahatma Gandhi’s teachings on non-violence and truth, saying, “Bapu taught us exactly this - speak the truth, fight peacefully.And that's what scares this government the most.”“Because a lathi can stop a crowd, but not a question. Gyanesh Kumar will go. And the system that put him there will go too,” he added.Opposition parties and student organisations attempted to gather near Jantar Mantar in Delhi, with the AAP, All India Students' Association (AISA), Students' Federation of India (SFI), National Students' Union of India (NSUI), Indian Youth Congress (IYC) and other youth groups demanding Kumar’s resignation.According to news agency PTI, around 700 protesters were detained by Delhi Police. Protesters were stopped at several points, including Firoz Shah Road and Ashoka Road, as they tried to proceed towards Jantar Mantar.AAP leaders Saurabh Bharadwaj, Atishi and Sanjeev Jha were among those detained, while Rajya Sabha MP Sanjay Singh was stopped on his way to the protest. Internet services were suspended in central Delhi and entry and exit gates at 12 metro stations, including Rajiv Chowk and Central Secretariat, were closed as part of security arrangements.SFI general secretary Aishe Ghosh said activists of the SFI and Democratic Youth Federation of India were also detained. AAP leaders alleged that police action would not stop their campaign.“We are protesting because the EC is responsible for protecting the sanctity of every vote. When questions are being raised within the commission itself over decisions concerning the electoral roll, the country deserves answers and accountability,” IYC president Uday Bhanu Chib said, according to PTI.Protests were also held at Mumbai’s Shivaji Park, where thousands attended a demonstration organised by the Cockroach Janata Party (CJP) and other groups seeking Kumar’s resignation.CJP leader Abhijeet Dipke warned of “Jantar Mantar 2.0” if Kumar did not step down, while party leader Ajinkya Shinde demanded his resignation and criminal proceedings. The CJP also called for the freezing of the 2025 voter lists and the abolition of the 2023 law governing the appointment of election commissioners.Dipke made several allegations concerning voter deletions and additions across states, including Maharashtra, Delhi, Tamil Nadu and West Bengal. These claims were made by him during the protest and were not independently established in the supplied reports.The protests came after an Indian Express report claimed that election commissioners Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi had raised objections at least 14 times over 10 months on decisions and procedures linked to the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) exercise and other electoral matters.The Election Commission rejected the suggestion that these objections represented institutional dissent, saying operational queries, inputs and suggestions during the draft stage were part of its normal administrative and decision-making process.The ECI said decisions on the SIR schedule were unanimous.The opposition’s campaign is expected to continue, with further programmes planned, including one on October 6 and a major rally in Delhi on November 1.
Article Summary: Rahul gandhi hits out at centre amid protests against cec, invokes mahatma gandhi. Around 700 detained in delhi amid alleged irregularities in the electoral-roll revision exercise. Opposition parties, student groups and civil society organisations held protests in delhi and mumbai.

Article Title: 'May Bapu’s timeless message keep guiding us': PM Modi pays tribute to Mahatma Gandhi, attends prayer meet

PM Modi attending interfaith prayer meeting, pays floral tributes to Mahatma Gandhi at Gandhi Smriti

NEW DELHI: Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Friday attended a special interfaith prayer meeting at Gandhi Smriti in New Delhi on the occasion of Mahatma Gandhi 's birth anniversary, where he paid floral tributes to the Father of the Nation.Earlier in the day, PM Modi paid floral tributes to Gandhi at Rajghat and former Prime Minister Lal Bahadur Shastri at Vijay Ghat to mark their respective birth anniversaries. In a post on X, the Prime Minister had further said the lives of Gandhi and Shastri, marked by “simplicity, courage and service to the nation”, continue to inspire generations. He said their ideals and commitment to India's progress would remain a guiding light.PM had earlier paid tribute to Gandhi on his 157th birth anniversary and called for greater adoption of Swadeshi, with Khadi at the forefront. He urged people to buy at least one Khadi product on October 2 and take pride in calling it Swadeshi.“May Bapu’s timeless message keep guiding us towards a better society and a Viksit Bharat,” he said.Several other leaders also paid tribute to Gandhi and Shastri in the Central Hall of Samvidhan Sadan.Lok Sabha Speaker Om Birla, Defence Minister Rajnath Singh, Union ministers JP Nadda and Kiren Rijiju, Leader of Opposition in Rajya Sabha Mallikarjun Kharge and Leader of Opposition in Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi were among those present.Meanwhile, school students and artists performed devotional bhajans during the prayer meeting. Vice President CP Radhakrishnan also attended the programme and paid floral tributes to Gandhi, remembering his role in India's freedom movement and his message of harmony and social upliftment.READ ALSO: Gandhi Jayanti: Mamata says stronger India must be guided Bapu’s ideals Gandhi was born on October 2, 1869, in Porbandar, Gujarat. His birth anniversary is observed as Gandhi Jayanti , while the United Nations observes October 2 as the International Day of Non-Violence.Shastri was born on October 2, 1904, in Mughalsarai, Uttar Pradesh, and served as prime minister from 1964 to 1966. He is remembered for the slogan “Jai Jawan, Jai Kisan” and his emphasis on self-reliance and the agricultural sector.

Article Title: Protests against CEC Gyanesh Kumar: Over 700 detained in Delhi, thousands attend CJP stir in Mumbai - top developments
Article Text:
Protesters stage a protest under the leadership of CJP Founder Abhijeet Dipke, seeking CEC Gyanesh Kumar's resignation over voter roll deletions at Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj Park, Dadar, in Mumbai (ANI Photo)

AISA’s Neha Bora calls for protesters to return

Protesters stopped at barricades, metro services hit

Thousands gather at Mumbai’s Shivaji Park

Police restrictions in Delhi, Mumbai

Why protesters are demanding Kumar’s resignation

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Protests demanding the resignation of chief election commissioner Gyanesh Kumar intensified across Delhi and Mumbai on Friday, with around 700 people detained in the national capital and thousands gathering at Mumbai’s Shivaji Park despite police denying permission for the demonstrations.The protests, involving opposition parties, student organisations and youth groups, centred on alleged irregularities in the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls and claims of mass voter deletions.In Delhi, AAP leaders Atishi, Saurabh Bharadwaj and Sanjeev Jha, AISA president Neha Bora, CPI(M) leaders M A Baby and Brinda Karat, CPI national secretary P Sandosh Kumar, RJD leader Manoj Jha, social activist Yogendra Yadav, DYFI president A A Rahim and former JNUSU president Aishe Ghosh were among those detained.Shortly after being detained, AISA national president Neha Bora urged protesters to return to Jantar Mantar and continue the demonstration.“All comrades, please return to Jantar Mantar and stand together for democracy and our right to vote. Do not be intimidated. Do not be silenced. Our peaceful protest continues,” Bora said.AAP’s Atishi, Sanjay Singh, Saurabh Bharadwaj and Sanjeev Jha were also detained as protesters attempted to reach Jantar Mantar.Bharadwaj was seen lying on the road while protesting against the police action.Atishi said the protesters were demonstrating peacefully to protect democracy and the right to vote.“When the British ruled India, Gandhiji fought for people's right to vote. Today, when we have that right, Gyanesh Kumar is trying to take it away,” she said.She later said protesters were taken away in buses and detained at the Fatehpur Beri police station.“We are not afraid of Modiji's police. We will continue to fight to protect the right to vote. The fight against vote theft will continue. The EC's system will have to be corrected and Gyanesh Kumar will have to resign,” Atishi said.Bharadwaj later said more than 500 people had reached Jantar Mantar before the scheduled protest and posted, “GenZ rocks.”Police said around 700 people were detained from Jantar Mantar and nearby areas. A police source told PTI that around 700 SFI members trying to reach Jantar Mantar at around 11 am were stopped at the Ashoka Road roundabout, with many detained.Protesters from the AAP, AISA, SFI, NSUI, IYC and other student and youth organisations attempted to move towards Jantar Mantar but were stopped at several locations, including Firoz Shah Road and Ashoka Road.Police repeatedly made public announcements asking people not to assemble at Jantar Mantar, saying no gathering had been permitted there.The protesters raised slogans including “Ek kachori, do samosa, Gyanesh tumhara kya bharosa” and “Gali gali mein shor hai, Modi-Gyanesh vote chor hai”, while placards carried messages such as “Resign Do”.The Indian Youth Congress marched from its office on Raisina Road towards Jantar Mantar, with protesters wearing masks bearing the faces of Kumar and Prime Minister Narendra Modi.IYC president Uday Bhanu Chib said the Election Commission was responsible for protecting the sanctity of every vote.“We are protesting because the EC is responsible for protecting the sanctity of every vote. When questions are being raised within the commission itself over decisions concerning the electoral roll, the country deserves answers and accountability,” Chib said.The Delhi Metro said entry and exit gates at 12 stations were closed during the day as part of security arrangements. These included Rajiv Chowk, Central Secretariat and Janpath. Internet services were also suspended in central Delhi.AAP’s Rajya Sabha MP Sanjay Singh was stopped at North Avenue while heading towards the protest and later said he was sitting on a dharna in front of the Mahatma Gandhi statue on the Parliament premises against “vote theft”.Bharadwaj questioned the need for permission to protest at Jantar Mantar, saying the AAP had submitted letters seeking permission around six days earlier and claimed that police had not taken a decision.In Mumbai, thousands attended a protest organised by the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) at Shivaji Park, despite police denying permission for the gathering.CJP leader Abhijeet Dipke warned of “Jantar Mantar 2.0” if Kumar did not resign and called for a nationwide mobilisation.“If Gyanesh Kumar does not resign, the Gen Z of the entire nation will go to Delhi. There will be Jantar Mantar 2.0,” Dipke said, giving a call for “Chalo Delhi”.CJP leader Ajinkya Shinde demanded Kumar’s resignation and criminal proceedings. The party also called for the freezing of the 2025 voter lists and the abolition of the 2023 law laying down the procedure for appointing Election Commissioners.Dipke also said, “Appointment of CEC should be transparent; there should be involvement of civil society.”Protesters carrying tricolours and placards with messages including “Gyanesh BRO, JUST RESIGN” and “Gaddaar Gyaanu Must Go” gathered in the area.Veteran actors Naseeruddin Shah and Shabana Azmi, filmmakers Vishal Bhardwaj and Hansal Mehta, singer-music director Vishal Dadlani and Tushar Gandhi, Mahatma Gandhi’s great-grandson, were present at the Mumbai protest.The Shiv Sena (UBT) extended support to the agitation, while the Maharashtra Navnirman Sena (MNS) also supported the CJP’s protest.Police in both Delhi and Mumbai had denied permission for the proposed protests.In Delhi, prohibitory orders under Section 163 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita were in force across the New Delhi district, restricting public meetings or assemblies of five or more people, processions, demonstrations, picketing and dharnas without prior written permission.The Delhi Police said the restrictions were imposed to ensure public safety, maintain public order and facilitate smooth traffic movement.In Mumbai, police said they were not authorised to permit the Shivaji Park gathering in view of a 2013 Bombay High Court order and described the area as a silence zone.Despite the restrictions, protesters reached Shivaji Park, while police and security forces were deployed in large numbers and routes from Dadar railway station were barricaded.The agitation intensified after media reports claimed that Election Commissioners Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi had recorded objections on at least 14 occasions over 10 months concerning decisions and procedures related to the SIR exercise and other electoral matters.The reported objections included issues concerning voter deletions, Form 6 and access to electoral-roll databases.The Election Commission rejected the suggestion that the objections amounted to institutional dissent, saying operational queries, inputs and suggestions raised during the draft stage were part of its standard administrative and decision-making process. The ECI said the three-member commission had taken all decisions, including those relating to the SIR, unanimously.The protests were part of a wider mobilisation by political parties, student organisations and youth groups. Demonstrations were also reported in Ahmedabad, Lucknow and Patna.AAP national media in-charge Anurag Dhanda said the party would continue its campaign.“We will not stop here. We will continue the protest across the country,” he said.CJP leader Saurav Das also criticised the detention of protesters in Delhi, saying, “Delhi Police has again resorted to brutality. We warn Delhi Police to improve or we will improve you.”
Article Summary: Around 700 people detained in delhi, thousands gather at mumbai's shivaji park. Demonstrations centred on alleged irregularities in the special intensive revision (sir) of electoral rolls. Aisa president neha bora urges protesters to return to jantar mantar.

Article Title: When the crew became the crisis: Air India’s 2009 mid-air brawl
Article Text:
A brawl 17 years ago brought into question flight safety

The flight carrying 106 passengers from Sharjah to Delhi via Lucknow witnessed a

mid-air confrontation

that raised questions about

cockpit discipline

and flight safety

A fight at 30,000 feet

From argument to violence

Investigations and fallout

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Read the detailed story

The recent flydubai incident has highlighted an unusual aviation danger: what happens when those responsible for flying an aircraft become part of the crisis themselves.Captain Smit Machchhar was reportedly attacked by his co-pilot during a flight, triggering a dangerous descent before the injured captain managed to open the cockpit door and allow others to intervene. The aircraft eventually landed safely.Seventeen years earlier, an Indian Airlines (then a subsidiary of Air India) flight witnessed a mid-air confrontation that raised similar questions about cockpit discipline and flight safety.On October 3, 2009, Indian Airlines flight IC-884 was carrying 106 passengers from Sharjah to Delhi via Lucknow. While cruising at around 30,000 feet over Pakistan, Captain Ranbir Arora and co-pilot Aditya Chopra became embroiled in a dispute with flight purser Amit Khanna and flight attendant Komal Singh.Reports said the confrontation spilled between the cockpit and galley while the Airbus A320 was airborne.The dispute had begun before take-off from Sharjah.In Sharjah, the cabin crew met Captain Ranbir Arora and co-pilot Aditya Chopra for a pre-flight briefing, during which the two sides were believed to have had an altercation.“The cabin crew lobby said that after the initial tension on the ground in Sharjah, when the woman crew member [Komal Singh] went into the cockpit, one of the pilots held her hand and then pushed her out of the cockpit,” according to a TOI report.She reportedly hit the cockpit door and began bleeding.Khanna then intervened, according to a cabin crew representative, who alleged that the pilots became abusive and fought with him.The pilots denied the allegation. They instead accused Khanna of misconduct that they claimed had compromised flight safety. The pilots also alleged that the molestation complaint was “aimed to protect the complainant’s purser friend — who has a commercial pilot licence (CPL) — from facing action”, the report added.After landing in Delhi, Singh filed a molestation complaint against the two pilots.There were also reports that the cockpit was briefly left effectively “unmanned” while the confrontation continued outside. Some accounts said Arora threatened to divert the aircraft to Karachi. These claims were not independently established.Singh’s allegations triggered a separate investigation. Air India set up a five-member committee, while the National Commission for Women formed a five-member panel.Delhi Police recorded Singh’s statement and registered a molestation case.Air India confirmed the fight and ordered an inquiry, while the Directorate General of Civil Aviation initiated a probe. All four crew members were grounded.The airline’s preliminary inquiry concluded that Arora and Khanna had played a greater role. Both were suspended, while Chopra and Singh remained grounded. The Indian Commercial Pilots Association questioned the action against Arora, saying the findings were not final.Air India later filed departmental chargesheets against all four. Singh was charged with participating in the altercation, failing to leave the cockpit when directed and speaking to the media in breach of company policy.Arora faced allegations including abusive language and pushing Khanna and Singh from the cockpit, while Khanna was accused of initiating the fight.An airline official said the preliminary inquiry found all four guilty of some charges, including conduct that tarnished the company's reputation.The episode became more than a workplace dispute. It showed how a personal conflict among crew members can spill into an aircraft's operational environment — and put flight safety under strain.
Article Summary: A brawl 17 years ago brought into question flight safety and cockpit discipline. Flight carrying 106 passengers from sharjah to delhi via lucknow witnessed a mid-air confrontation. Captain smit machchhar was reportedly attacked by his co-pilot during a flight, triggering a dangerous descent.

Article Title: 'I am Hanuman to Rahul Gandhi': Ajay Rai after being replaced as UP Congress chief

NEW DELHI: Former Uttar Pradesh Congress Committee (UPCC) president Ajay Rai on Saturday called himself a “Hanuman” to Congress leader Rahul Gandhi , saying he would continue to follow the party’s national leadership and carry out its political fight regardless of the position he holds."Whatever decision the national leadership makes. They told me to fight Modi, and I fought openly with full strength, and I will continue to fight. So whatever the national leadership decides, I stand by it. I am certainly a 'Hanuman' to my leader Rahul Gandhi; wherever he says, I will be there," he told ANI.Rai also recalled his contest against Prime Minister Narendra Modi in the 2024 Lok Sabha elections from Varanasi. Describing himself as a “simple worker”, he said he had been fielded against PM Modi with the support of the Congress leadership and Rahul Gandhi.Rai made the remarks after the Congress appointed Aradhana Mishra ‘Mona’ as the new UP Congress president, replacing him as part of an organisational reshuffle ahead of the 2027 Uttar Pradesh assembly elections. Speaking to reporters, Rai said he had always followed the decisions of the national leadership and would continue to do so."A simple worker like me was fielded against Prime Minister Narendra Modi. With the support of the top leadership and Rahul Gandhi, we secured 4.6 lakh votes in Varanasi and defeated PM Modi in seven rounds. I thank Rahul Gandhi and the top leadership for their faith in me and extend my best wishes to Aradhana Mishra Mona. I hope she works hard, takes the party forward and strengthens the trust of workers by standing with them against oppression and injustice," he said.Rai said political positions were temporary and pointed to his record as a five-time MLA from Pindra. He said he had worked extensively for people in his constituency and recalled arranging blood donations when required."Positions in politics come and go. I have been an MLA from Pindra five times and have worked extensively for the people, even arranging blood donations through my family when needed. I thank the Pradesh Congress Committee employees, drivers, staff, workers and supporters who stood by me around the clock and helped me throughout my journey across Uttar Pradesh. We have always stood against oppression and injustice wherever it occurred," he said.Meanwhile, Mishra, after taking charge as the new UP Congress president, said the party was ready for the 2027 Assembly elections and would contest them with the INDIA alliance."Today marks the beginning of a new dawn. I express my gratitude to my leadership for entrusting me with this responsibility. This is a big challenge; time is short, and every Congress worker will have to work. Together, we must work with full strength," she said.Mishra also highlighted the Congress’ focus on women’s empowerment, saying, "If there's anyone who is the biggest example of 'Beti Hun, Lad Sakti Hun', it is me."She recalled the party’s decision under Priyanka Gandhi Vadra’s leadership to field 40% women candidates in the 2022 Uttar Pradesh Assembly elections."Before this, under Priyanka Gandhi's leadership, we fielded 40% women candidates with tickets in the 2022 elections. It is evident today that the Congress Party has always worked for the empowerment of women," she said."We are ready for the 2027 elections, and the INDIA alliance will contest the elections with full strength. We will fight the elections with the entire alliance," the newly appointed UP Congress chief said.

He said political positions were temporary and pointed to his record as a five-time mla from pindra. Mishra, after taking charge, said the party was ready for the 2027 assembly elections.

NEW DELHI: Amid a drought situation in his home state of Karnataka, Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge on Saturday wrote to Prime Minister Narendra Modi , listing six demands and stressing that the BJP-led Centre and the Congress-led state government must “rise above their differences” in view of the situation.“The state is facing one of its gravest drought situations in recent years, with a 58% rainfall deficiency as of September, widespread crop losses and severe distress for lakhs of farming families,” Kharge wrote on X, sharing his letter.He said the Karnataka government had sought Rs 3,705.30 crore in assistance under the National Disaster Response Fund (NDRF) and State Disaster Response Fund (SDRF) framework against estimated losses of Rs 18,748.23 crore.Kharge’s six demands are:“Drought relief is a humanitarian imperative and must rise above political differences between the Centre and the state. I hope the Government of India will act with urgency and compassion and extend timely assistance to Karnataka, providing much-needed sustenance, fodder, water and livelihood security to millions of affected citizens,” Kharge said.He added that he had also written to Union Home minister Amit Shah seeking the same intervention.Karnataka has been seeking central assistanch amid a worsening drought situation. Recent reports said the state had declared 177 taluks drought-affected, while ground-truthing was underway in additional areas. The state had initially sought Rs 3,705.30 crore for the 101 drought-affected taluks.
Article Summary: Mallikarjun kharge writes to pm modi asking for help in his home state of karnataka. He says the state is facing one of its gravest drought situations in recent years. Karnataka has been seeking central assistanch amid a worsening drought situation.
